messages:
maria gomez: FYI I ran the prefill-heavy replay overnight against the new kernel-selection logic. Saw consistent latency bump for long-context (>32k) traces, ~12-18% p95 reg.
ben park: ugh. which kernel path was picked? was it the fused-attn fallback?
yukiko tanaka: looks like kernel-v2 is getting chosen for prefill but kernel-v1 was previously used. profiling shows more memory copy stalls during KV flush.
sahil rao: can you paste the trace snippet? also whether batching heuristics changed at the same time.
maria gomez: trace excerpt:
```
[2026-03-17T02:14:55Z] prefill_start seq=40960 model=gpt-open-16b
selected_kernel: kernel-v2
batching_window_ms: 10
kv_cache_activations: flush @ 64k
latency_breakdown_ms: prefill=136.4 kv_copy=24.8 decode=6.1
```
ciara: that kv_copy seems high. did we disable async memcpy for that kernel?
yukiko tanaka: kernel-v2 currently uses a different tile layout; async memcpy not yet wired for the new code path. that explains the extra kv_copy time.
ben park: okay actionable: 1) try forcing kernel-v1 for prefill-heavy runs to confirm. 2) re-run replay vs synthetic with same seqlen distribution.
sahil rao: I'll run a 6h replay with kernel override. command I'm using:
```
./harness/replay_runner --trace-root=/tmp/replay --scale=4 --force-kernel=kernel-v1 --kv-warm=off
```
maria gomez: also want to compare synthetic mix: run synthetic generator with our observed seqlen histogram (attached) so it's apples-to-apples on distribution parity.
ciara: small note: our batching heuristic changed last deploy to prefer larger batches when prefill ratio > 0.7. could be increasing queuing for prefill windows.
yukiko tanaka: right — for prefill-dominant workloads we should bias to smaller batch caps to avoid one big prefill delaying others.
ben park: for methodology we should standardize a 3-stage test: cold-kv replay, warm-kv replay, synthetic-matched-histogram. capture p50/p95/p99 and memory copy counters.
sahil rao: initial run forced kernel-v1: no regression, p95 back to baseline. confirms kernel-v2 memcpy is culprit.
maria gomez: can we quick patch kernel-v2 to use async memcpy? yukiko volunteer?
yukiko tanaka: I'll prototype a minimal async memcpy hook today, push a branch. ping @ciara for CI perf runs.
ciara: will queue a canary load job. Deploy-bot: please schedule eng-runtime/canary/perf at 02:30 UTC
deploy-bot: Scheduled job eng-runtime/canary/perf at 2026-03-18T02:30:00Z :white_check_mark:
ben park: after fix, re-run both replay and synthetic-matched. also add a checkpoint for KV occupancy (percent of cache filled) — might influence kernel selection.
maria gomez: agreed. let's capture kernel decision trace for each request (add header: X-Kernel-Decision) so we can correlate.
sahil rao: note for benchmarking notes doc: mention prefill-dominant workloads are more sensitive to memcpy and tile layout than decode path; add guidance to prefer kernels with async memcpy for >16k prefills.
yukiko tanaka: rough ETA for patch: EOD PT. will open PR and tag this thread.
maria gomez: thanks — will add the perf graphs to the replay run ticket once CI finishes. :thumbsup:
